title: Chip dataset summary
description: What a chipping run produced, as printed by `umbra chips --json` (`umbra_py.chips.ChipDataset.to_dict`): where the tiles and their manifest are, how the grid was cut, which acquisitions are in it, what the conversion did, and — where a run had them to report — the roll-ups that say which scenes a correction should not be trusted on, which passes were left out, and what asking the archive first cost. The per-chip records live in the manifest this names, one `chip-record.schema.json` each.

out_dir.description: The directory the chips and manifest were written to.

manifest.description: The manifest file, or null when the run collected its records without writing one. Its extension chooses the format: `.jsonl` (one record per line), `.geojson` (a `FeatureCollection` of chip footprints) or `.parquet` (a stac-geoparquet table). Every one of them carries the same `chip-record.schema.json` record.

chip_count.description: How many tiles were written — the length of the manifest.

chip_size.description: The tile edge in pixels. Partial edge tiles are dropped, so every chip is exactly this square.

stride.description: The step between tile origins in pixels. Equal to `chip_size` for a non-overlapping grid, smaller for overlapping tiles.

units.description: What a pixel value is on the scale the chips were written at.

format.description: The chip file format. `npy` is a bare float32 array, so its geo metadata lives only in the manifest.

item_count.description: How many acquisitions contributed chips — the length of `items`. Lower than the selection when tiles were dropped by `--min-valid` or a pass was skipped.

items.description: The acquisition ids present in the manifest, sorted. The unit to split a train/test set on: two chips of one scene are not independent samples.

license.description: The source data's licence (design principle 4: attribution survives every transformation, including into a training set).

conversion.description: Present only when a complex product was geocoded for this run (`--asset SICD`), so an ordinary raster run's payload does not carry the key at all.

noise.description: Present only when some scene in the run had a noise floor subtracted.

speckle.description: Present only when some scene in the run was speckle-filtered.

clip.description: Present only when the run was clipped to an area of interest (`--clip-bbox`).

skipped_count.description: How many acquisitions were left out. Present only with `skipped`, and only when there was a hole: a run that included everything it was offered is unchanged by this key existing.

skipped.description: The passes the run could not include, each in the product's own words. Present only when there was one, which is what makes its absence a statement rather than a default.

skipped_manifest.description: Where that hole was also written — the `skipped.jsonl` sidecar beside the manifest, so a loader reading the directory sees it too. Present only when the sidecar was actually written, since a run that kept its records without a manifest has the hole in this payload and nowhere on disk.

preflight.description: Present only when the run read the archive's headers before downloading anything (`--preflight`).

conversion.title: SICD conversion settings
conversion.description: How each complex product was geocoded before it was chipped (`umbra_py.chips.SicdConversion`). Every field is passed straight to `umbra_py.convert.sicd_to_geocoded_cog` and means what it means there. These are the settings *requested*; what actually ran is read back per chip from the converted raster's own tags into `chip-record.schema.json`.

dem.description: The elevation model used for orthorectification, `auto` to fetch the window's tiles, or null for the flat-earth geocoding.

rtc_model.description: Which flattening model. Only `facet` measures layover.

calibration.description: The radiometric calibration asked for, or null for relative amplitude. Composes with the flattening, both being power-domain factors, so `facet` + `gamma0` is a terrain-flattened gamma-nought product.

noise_subtract.description: Whether the receiver's own noise floor was taken off detected power before anything scaled it.

noise_model.description: Where that floor came from. `measured` reads the product's own `NoisePoly` and is the only one that can be refused for want of metadata; the two inferred models read the scene's dark tail instead.

speckle_filter.description: The speckle filter applied in image space before geocoding, or null when none was.

resolution.description: The output pixel size in metres, or null to take it from the product.

gcp_grid.description: The edge of the control-point grid the geocoding is fitted through.

bbox.description: The area of interest as `[min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat]`, or null for the whole collect. A clip chooses *which* ground is written rather than how finely it is sampled — the pixel size still comes from the whole input.

noise.title: Noise-subtraction roll-up
noise.description: What the noise subtraction did across the run (`umbra_py.chips.NoiseSummary`). The question it answers is not 'what was the floor' but **were any of these scenes ones the estimator should not have been used on** — the inferred floors work because a scene's dark surfaces are a different population from its backscatter, and where they are not, the subtraction takes real backscatter off. Counted per *acquisition*, since the numbers describe the scene a chip was cut from; counting chips would weight a wide scene more heavily for no reason.

scenes.description: Acquisitions in the run whose chips carry a noise subtraction.

models.description: The distinct floors used, sorted — normally one, since a run converts every scene the same way. More than one means the dataset mixes measurements that must not be differenced against each other.

margin_scenes.description: How many of `scenes` reported a margin at all. Only the inferred floors do: a measured floor assumes nothing about the scene, so it has nothing to report.

low_margin_scenes.description: How many of `margin_scenes` sat below `margin_warn_db` — the scenes with too little dark ground to read. This is the number the roll-up exists for. Never a refusal: a uniformly bright scene is legitimate imagery, and the honest fix there is a measured floor.

margin_warn_db.description: The advisory threshold applied (`umbra_py.convert.NOISE_MARGIN_WARN_DB`), so a consumer can re-apply its own without knowing the constant.

min_margin_db.description: The narrowest margin in the batch — the worst scene. Null when no scene reported one.

max_floored_fraction.description: The largest fraction of a scene the floor drove to the sensor's sensitivity limit. Reported by both models.

speckle.title: Speckle-filtering roll-up
speckle.description: What the speckle filter did across the run (`umbra_py.chips.SpeckleSummary`) — the same shape as the noise roll-up, for the same reason. The question is **did the window buy anything, and on how many of these scenes did it not**: a filter's job is to raise the equivalent number of looks, and the honest report of that is the ratio, since both levels read low on a textured scene. Counted per acquisition. Never a refusal — a small gain on a textured scene is the outcome rather than a fault.

scenes.description: Acquisitions in the run whose chips were speckle-filtered.

filters.description: The distinct filters used, sorted — normally one.

windows.description: The distinct window edges used, sorted. With `filters` this is what says the dataset's resolution as opposed to its pixel size.

gain_scenes.description: How many of `scenes` reported an equivalent number of looks either side of the filter, so a gain could be computed at all. A scene smaller than one measuring block, or with too little finite ground, reports neither.

low_gain_scenes.description: How many of `gain_scenes` came out below `gain_warn` — where the resolution the window spent bought little. This is the number the roll-up exists for.

min_gain.description: The worst `enl_after / enl_before` in the batch. Null when no scene reported a pair.

median_gain.description: The typical one. Null on the same condition.

clip.title: Clip roll-up
clip.description: What a `--clip-bbox` run read instead of the whole scene, across the batch (`umbra_py.chips.ClipSummary`) — the batch form of the `clipped` line `umbra convert --clip-bbox` prints. The question it answers is **was pointing the run at an area of interest worth it, and by how much**, and the honest figure is the ratio of what was read to what a whole-scene run would have read. Counted per acquisition, like the noise and speckle roll-ups. Unlike them it is *accumulated* during the run rather than derived from the records: the clip saving is deliberately not a `chip-record.schema.json` field (a clip changes which ground is written, which the transform already states, not what a pixel value means), so there is nothing in the manifest to derive it from.

scenes.description: Acquisitions in the run whose read was clipped to the area of interest. A scene whose clip covered the whole product still counts — its fraction is what says the clip bought nothing there, not its absence.

window_pixels.description: Pixels actually read, summed across `scenes` — what the clipped run cost.

scene_pixels.description: Pixels the whole products hold, summed — what an unclipped run would have cost.

fraction.description: The batch's `window_pixels / scene_pixels` — the headline saving. 0 when the clipped scenes hold no pixels.

min_fraction.description: The smallest per-scene `window / scene` ratio in the batch.

max_fraction.description: The largest per-scene ratio. With `min_fraction` it tells a run that clipped evenly from one that read most of some passes and little of others.

preflight.title: Preflight roll-up
preflight.description: What asking the archive first cost this run, and what it saved (`umbra_py.chips.PreflightSummary`). The per-acquisition verdicts behind it are `preflight.schema.json`; this is the batch's summary of them.

checked.description: How many acquisitions' metadata was read over the wire.

supported.description: How many cleared the run's own conversion settings and went on to be downloaded.

skipped.description: How many were dropped before a download — the refusals plus `missing`. They appear in the payload's `skipped` array with `stage` = `preflight`.

unreadable.description: How many reads failed on the *wire*. Those passes are **kept**: a transport failure is not a product saying it cannot answer, and dropping a scene over a blip would be exactly the silent hole this design avoids.

missing.description: How many reads failed on the *product*: nothing at the href, or something at it that is not a readable SICD. Final, so those passes are dropped and counted in `skipped`. Counted apart from `unreadable` because only one of the two is worth asking about again.

bytes_read.description: What the whole check cost: product headers and SICD XML, tens of kilobytes each.

product_bytes_skipped.description: The download the check removed — the dropped products, summed, as their own sources declared them. Deliberately narrow: a supported pass is downloaded anyway, so its header read is pure overhead and only the dropped passes are a saving. Null when no dropped source stated a size.
